Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Internal and external candidates will be considered for this vacancy. For the purposes of this vacancy, internal candidates are defined as staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded or ungraded contract, including Junior Professional Officers (JPOs), staff on Special Leave Without Pay (SLWOP), UN Volunteers with at least twelve (12) months of continuous service in IOM, and staff members on secondment/loan released by the Organization, unless otherwise specified in their contract. Staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded contract will not retain their contract type if appointed to an ungraded position. Organizational Context and Scope Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission and the direct supervision of the designated programme or migration health supervisor, with technical supervision from the Chief Migration Health Officer or Regional Health Assessment Programme Coordinator, the incumbent will conduct migration health assessment activities and provide medical support for AVRR cases. The physician will ensure that clinical assessments, documentation, referrals, fitness-to-travel decisions, medical travel arrangements and continuity-of-care planning are completed in line with applicable IOM, donor and destination-country requirements. Responsibilities Conduct migration health assessments, including medical history, physical examination and review of available clinical records. Arrange or review required investigations, including laboratory testing, imaging and other examinations, according to applicable programme and destination-country requirements. Identify health conditions requiring treatment, referral, stabilization or follow-up, and coordinate care with relevant health facilities and treating physicians. Support vaccination, tuberculosis management, pre-departure medical procedures and other health interventions in accordance with applicable protocols. Ensure correct identification of migrants and complete, accurate and timely medical documentation, certification and data entry in relevant IOM systems. Review AVRR cases with known or suspected medical conditions and assess decision-making capacity, fitness to travel and medical feasibility of return, as applicable. Recommend additional assessment or stabilization when the available information is insufficient to confirm safe travel. Determine required medical travel conditions, such as medical or non-medical escort, wheelchair, additional seats, stretcher, oxygen, medications, medical supplies or family support. Review proposed itineraries from a medical perspective and complete airline medical forms, including MEDA or MEDIF, when required. Coordinate with AVRR, Operations, Migration Health and relevant counterparts in the country of return to support safe travel and continuity of care after arrival. Brief medical escorts on the case and travel management plan, coordinate required escort supplies, and review escort reports and travel-related incidents. Apply infection prevention and control, patient safety, confidentiality, informed consent and ethical standards throughout service delivery. Contribute to quality assurance through case review, record checks, data analysis, incident follow-up and implementation of applicable SOPs. Maintain case records and relevant statistics, and prepare routine or ad hoc reports requested by the supervisor. Perform other related duties as assigned. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education University degree in Medicine from an accredited academic institution. Valid licence to practise medicine in the duty-station country is mandatory. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience At least two years of relevant professional clinical experience, preferably in emergency medicine, internal medicine or a multidisciplinary hospital setting. Experience conducting medical assessments, preparing medical reports and coordinating referrals or patient care. Experience in migration health, humanitarian health, resettlement health or AVRR programming is desirable. Experience with fitness-to-travel assessment, medical movement support or continuity-of-care planning is an advantage. Skills Good knowledge of clinical medicine, patient safety and infection prevention and control. Ability to make sound clinical decisions and clearly document the rationale for recommendations. Strong coordination and communication skills, including liaison with health facilities, operations teams and cross-border counterparts. Understanding of in-flight physiology or aviation medicine is an advantage. Good organizational skills, attention to detail and ability to respond flexibly to operational needs. Languages All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish). Required For this position, fluency in English and French is required (oral and written). DESIRABLE Working kwnoledge of Arabic is an advantage Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators (applicable only if with direct reports) Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential. Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty. Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction. Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings. Notes Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. review_candidates.description: Vacature Wat ga je doen Opdrachtomschrijving Rijkswaterstaat werkt aan projecten door middel van het Integraalprojectmanagementmodel(IPM model). Je maakt deel uit van een projectteam waarbij jij borgt dat het team op basis van de juiste informatie beslissingen neemt. Daartoe lever je waardevolle stuur-, beheers- en verantwoordingsinformatie aan projectteamleden en de sturingslijn. Als manager projectbeheersing verzorg jij de integrale beheersing voor onderhoudscontracten. Hierbij vul je zelfstandig de integrale beheersing in (scope, tijd, geld, risico’s, planning, informatie, kwaliteit en documentatie) voor één of meerdere contracten. Je creëert overzicht en brengt blinde vlekken binnen de projectbeheersing onder de aandacht. Dit doe je onder meer door de verschillende projectbeheersingsaspecten en de samenhang daartussen te analyseren en te agenderen. Je bevindingen vertaal je naar heldere voorstellen tot besluitvorming. Hierbij stel je vanuit de projectopdracht duidelijke prioriteiten en doelen. Jij bewaakt samen met jouw collega’s vanuit de afdeling projectbeheersing bij Programma’s, Projecten en Onderhoud (PPO) de kwaliteit en de tijdige levering van die projectbeheersingsproducten. Jij houdt van het dragen van veel verantwoordelijkheid en dat is maar goed ook. Wanneer planningen afwijken, hangt het hele projectteam namelijk op jou. Je gedijt goed in de dynamische omgeving van Rijkswaterstaat. Juist daar zorg jij voor stabiliteit en overzicht. Verder ben je een echte aanvoerder die geniet van deze manager rol. Je teamleden op de hoogte houden van wat er speelt en ze in positie brengen, gaat je daardoor gemakkelijk af. Af en toe wat weerstand hoort er wat jou betreft bij. Dit omdraaien naar enthousiasme is iets waar jij juist energie van krijgt en het team natuurlijk ook. Je wordt Manager Projectbeheersing binnen het cluster B-Bruggen van Zee en Delta. Dit cluster werkt aan het onderhoud en de vernieuwing van verschillende vaste en beweegbare bruggen in Zeeland. De opgave bestaat uit projecten die al in uitvoering zijn, projecten die nog worden voorbereid en een nieuwe raamovereenkomst voor het onderhoud en de vernieuwing van beweegbare bruggen. Het cluster is relatief nieuw. Dat betekent dat de projectbeheersing nog verder moet worden opgebouwd en ingericht. Daar ligt voor jou een belangrijke opdracht. Je brengt structuur aan en zorgt samen met je team voor een samenhangende werkwijze voor onder andere planning, financiën, risico’s, kwaliteit, informatie en voortgang. Je bepaalt welke stuurinformatie nodig is, richt de bijbehorende processen in en zorgt ervoor dat het IPM-team tijdig over betrouwbare informatie beschikt om besluiten te kunnen nemen. Je stapt dus niet in een volledig ingerichte omgeving. Je krijgt juist de ruimte en verantwoordelijkheid om de projectbeheersing vanaf de basis verder op te bouwen. Daarbij geef je richting aan de professionals binnen projectbeheersing, breng je de verschillende disciplines bij elkaar en zorg je dat afspraken en werkwijzen daadwerkelijk worden toegepast. Je signaleert waar beheersing onvoldoende is ingericht en neemt het initiatief om dit te verbeteren. Dit vraagt om iemand die overzicht houdt, structuur aanbrengt en tegelijkertijd pragmatisch kan handelen. Je kunt schakelen tussen de dagelijkse praktijk van de projecten en de informatie die nodig is voor besluitvorming binnen Rijkswaterstaat. Daarmee lever je direct een bijdrage aan het beheerst onderhouden en vernieuwen van de bruggen in Zeeland. Wat wij aan jou waarderen Je bent samenwerkingsgericht en een voorbeeld in het tonen van eigenaarschap. Hierbij toon je respect voor anderen. Flexibel als je bent, pas je in iedere situatie de juiste aanpak toe. Je bent kritisch op jezelf en staat open voor feedback. Ruimte voor het opdoen van nieuwe kennis en ervaring? Die pak jij met beide handen aan. Doel van de opdracht Projectbeheersing conform de interne handreikingen en kaders. Over De Klant Rijkswaterstaat Rijkswaterstaat is de uitvoeringsorganisatie van het ministerie van Infrastructuur en Waterstaat en werkt dagelijks aan een veilig, leefbaar en bereikbaar Nederland. review_candidates.title: Director, Translation Programs & Capital Engagement
review_candidates.description: About The Engine As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit and public benefit organization, The Engine supports Tough Tech founders working to solve the world’s most pressing challenges in climate, health, and advanced systems. We do this through powerful founder programs, access to shared infrastructure and labs, and by convening a national network of corporate partners, investors, and experts. About The Builder Platform In September 2023, the National Science Foundation selected The Engine to stand up The Builder Platform (TBP) to be a model for post-award support, catalyze commercialization of groundbreaking scientific and technological advancements, and spur regional economic development across two cohorts of NSF Regional Innovation Engine (NSF Engine) awardees. The Builder Platform is a human-centered network that exists to support awardee regions in capitalizing on this high-impact investment, deploying consultative, programmatic, and community support across key stakeholders in their ecosystems. Bringing together the brightest minds in Tough Tech, The Builder Platform connects regional ecosystem builders to the capital, partners, tools and support they need to scale. Our tailored support is fueling the growth of ecosystems supported by the NSF Regional Innovation Engines program - a flagship initiative that is driving regional innovation across the country. The Builder Platform amplifies NSF's investments in regional innovation ecosystems, providing: Peer learning environments, Private sector network connections, Full lifecycle support from early R&D to full-scale technology deployment in critical technology sectors. The Builder Platform helps teams navigate microvalleys, reducing friction between stages, and accelerating the translation of breakthrough technologies. Learn more about The Builder Platform and the NSF Regional Innovation Engines we serve at builderplatform.engine.xyz. About The Role We are seeking a relationship-driven “Navigator” who also builds programs and capital connections for NSF Engines. Based at The Engine, this role serves as Navigator for multiple Cohort 2 NSF Engines, co-leads TBP's translation programming with responsibility for curriculum development/customization and delivery, and builds the NSF Engines Network of Networks for investment and capital. Its audience is the NSF Engines: their R&D and translation leads, ecosystem builders, and the PIs and researchers in their regions. Being based at The Engine lets this role partner directly with The Engine's team and bring its programs, investor network, and expertise to the NSF Engines. Reports to: Executive Director, The Builder Platform Key Responsibilities Engine Navigator Role Serve as the lead point of contact ("Navigator") for multiple Cohort 2 NSF Engines, actively managing relationships through regular check-ins with their CEOs and teams and facilitating essential connections. Identify each Engine's priority needs and match them to TBP resources, advisors, and programming. Deploy the Navigator practice's shared tools, playbooks, and cadence to the NSF Engines while continuously updating the tools in an ongoing fashion.. Translation Curriculum (Co-Lead) Co-lead TBP's translation programming, partnering with The Engine’s VP of Tech Translation/Ecosystem Development and The Builder Platform’s Sr Manager of Startup and Venture Ecosystem Development on curriculum development and delivery: building the content, adapting it to each NSF Engine's context (20 NSF Engines in the portfolio), and delivering it in-region. Design and deliver curriculum that helps NSF Engines and their associated institutions and personnel move research into the market. Targeted audiences include R&D and translation leads, ecosystem builders, and the PIs and researchers in their regions. Deliver curriculum through topical webinars, roundtables, office hours, small-group problem-solving sessions, and in-region workshops. Create content, templates, and tools for these audiences, bringing in pillar partners and TBP advisors as speakers and experts, and turn what works into reusable TBP resources/assets. Work with TBP's programming lead on calendar and format, and track outcomes (participation, follow-on engagement, Engine feedback) to improve each program. Investor & Capital Engagement Own TBP's investment and capital work stream, working closely with The Engine's team, including the Director of Partnerships, to bring The Engine's investor network and investor-focused programming to the NSF Engines. Cultivate and manage relationships with a curated network of Seed to Series B investors (angels, institutional VCs, corporate venture, and accelerators/incubators) with a clear mandate for Tough Tech. Connect NSF Engines' own investor networks to The Engine's to create a network of networks. Collaborate with NSF and NSF Engines on a National Investing Event. General Responsibilities Reporting & Metrics: Track and report key performance indicators for assigned Engines, programming, and investor engagement (e.g., investor meetings, introductions, funding rounds). Reporting: Contribute to Milestones reports, NSF deliverables, presentations, and other materials as needed. Data: Maintain accurate, up-to-date records across shared systems (Airtable, HubSpot, Circle, Monday) so the whole team can rely on a single source of truth. NSF Stakeholder Management: Participate in key meetings with NSF Leadership as a leading contributor, providing insight and data on the progress and needs of the Engines. Represent The Builder Platform at national events and conferences. Qualifications Experience: 7+ years in venture capital, startup or startup ecosystem work, technology commercialization or tech transfer, or program design, ideally in a technology-focused or mission-driven environment. Experience with Tough Tech, deep science, or university research is a significant advantage. Education: Bachelor's degree required. An MBA, a Master's or PhD in a technical/STEM field is a plus. Investor Network: A demonstrated, existing, and high-quality professional network among early-stage investors, corporate innovation leaders, and/or industry experts. Relationship Management: A track record of being a trusted point of contact for external partners or clients, with strong follow-through. Program Design: Experience designing and running programs, workshops, or curricula for researchers, founders, or ecosystem builders. Communication Skills: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to bridge the language gap between deep technical teams and business/financial stakeholders. Systems Fluency: Comfort working across tools like Airtable, HubSpot, Monday, and Circle (or similar platforms), with interest in using AI tools to improve team workflows. Soft Skills: Organized, results-oriented, a good listener, and an empathetic advocate for researchers, founders, and the ecosystems they work in. Travel Domestic travel: 25-30%, including some evenings and weekends as needed Why Join The Builder Platform? This is a chance to work at the front of a national innovation initiative from The Engine's home base. You'll advise NSF Engine leaders directly, connect their founders to investors, and build the programs that help researchers turn Tough Tech into companies in regions across the country. If you are mission-driven and want a role that combines relationship management, program building, and capital access, we encourage you to apply. We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.
